REPORTThe Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sports deals with the action taken by the Government on the Recommendations contained in its 349thReport on Demands for Grants 2023-24 of the Department of , which was presented to the Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 28th March, 2023.2. The Action Taken Notes in respect of Recommendations contained in above mentioned Report were received from the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education videtheir communication dated 4thJuly, 2023. These have been categorized as follows. Chapter I: Recommendations which have been accepted by the Government Paras3.1.8, 3.1.21, 3.2.11, 3.2.13, 4.2.4, Total - 5Chapter II: Recommendations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of Government's replies:-Paras2.9, 3.1.9, 3.1.12, 3.2.7, 3.3.7, 3.4.7, 3.4.8, 3.6.4, 3.7.5, 3.7.6, 4.1.4, 4.3.5,4.4.5Total - 13Chapter III: Recommendations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted by the Committee:-Paras- 3.1.14, 3.2.12, 3.5.3, 3.5.7, 4.3.7, 4.5.7Total - 6       Chapter-IV:  Recommendations in respect of which replies of the Government are still awaited:-Paras - NilTotal - Nil

2  
CHAPTER-IRECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENTOVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2023-24) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACYSAMAGRA SHIKSHA ABHIYANRecommendation1.The Committee appreciates the enhanced allocations under Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan which has witnessed increase of around 16% in BE 2023-24 as compared to RE 2022-23. The Committee suggests that mechanism for faster utilization should consistently be reviewed.(Para 3.1.8 of the 349thReport of the Committee)Action TakenThe Department has informed that with a view to have more effective cash management and bringing more efficiency in public expenditure management, Ministry of Finance (MoF)videits O.M. dated 23.03.2021 and 23.03.2022 has laid down guidelines which are to be followed by all the State Governments and Ministries/Departments of the Government of India regarding release and monitoring utilization of funds under Centrally Sponsored Schemes(CSS) effective from 01.07.2021. The fund transfer under the new procedure is through Single Nodal Account (SNA),which is operational in almost all States/UTs. The Department has interacted with States/UTs extensively for the effective implementation of this procedure. It was further informed that for ascertaining and ensuring the judicious use of funds released under Samagra Shiksha there are inbuilt checks, counter-checks and internal control systems as prescribed in the Manual on Financial Management and Procurement of Samagra Shiksha. There is also internal audit, statutory audit, concurrent audit and audit by State Accountant General. The Committee was also informed that the Department has launched Project Appraisal, Budgeting Achievements and Data Handling (PRABANDH) System. One of the important features of the PRABANDH System is regular updation of expenditure incurred under the different interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. For this purpose, a data visualization Dashboard has been created in the PRABANDH System for the display of monthly status of physical and financial progress under the major interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. The option for uploading 

3  
expenditures incurred by the National Component Agencies under Samagra Shiksha has also been enabled.Recommendation2.The Committee appreciates the increased budgetary allocations during 2023-24 against allocations of Rs. 5,326.36 crores in 2022-23 under Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) and also appreciates the efforts/initiatives taken for encouraging education among girl child. The Committee also appreciates the initiatives of the Department for taking up with the States for inclusion of proposals of vocational education in KGBVs in the Annual Work Plan and budget of Samagra Shiksha for consideration of Project Approval Boards meeting. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should accelerate the process of inclusion of the proposals of vocational education under KGBVs to ensure its inclusion at the earliest. The Department should also pursue for the coverage of KGBVs under hub and spoke model of vocational education under Samagra Shiksha 2.0.        (Para 3.1.21 ibid)Action TakenThe Department has informed that in pursuance of recommendations of NEP 2020, promoting vocationalization of education is one of the major objectives of Samagra Shiksha.  To widen the scope of employability to girls studying in KGBVs, the provision of vocationalization of secondary education under Samagra Shiksha has been extended to KGBVs also.  All States and UTs having KGBVs, have been requested to introduce vocational education in secondary and senior secondary classes in KGBVs and submit the Annual Work Plan and Budget of Samagra Shiksha for financial assistance for this component.It was also informed that Ministry of Education is providing funds for specific skill training in KGBVs, under which, States appoint vocational instructors in KGBVs to provide need based vocational education to girls.  Additionally, some of the States have started certificate based vocational courses in KGBVs under the provision of vocational education under Samagra Shiksha or through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS)/State agencies.  States/UTs have been asked to saturate all KGBVs with vocational education and the progress is monitored on a regular basis.

4  
PRADHAN MANTRIPOSHAN SHAKTI NIRMAN (PM POSHAN) SCHEMERecommendation3.   From analysis of Para 3.2.3 Table-14 (in 348thReport of the Committee EWCY&S) regarding details of enrolment of children and institutions for the years 2020-21 and 2021-22, it is encouragingly evident that there is increment in enrolment of children from 11.80 crores to 12.21 crores. This is indicative of a positive recovery from the perilous COVID-19 times and displays the that the Department should make sure even the increased number of enrolled students are covered under the blanket of PM POSHAN Scheme and make necessary augmentations in the budget allocation, student data and policy ambit.(Para 3.2.11 ibid)Action TakenThe Department has informed that States and UTs are being encouraged to cover all the enrolled students under the scheme as per norms. This issue was discussed in detail with States/UTsand they were advised to improve the coverage.It was also informed by the Department of School Education and Literacy that the National Food Security Act, 2013, Rules, Guidelines and Instructions issued under the PM POSHAN Scheme from time to time, provide that every child attending an eligible institution is to be covered under the Scheme and shall be served hot cooked meals or provided with Food Security Allowance, as applicable, on all school days. Further, States and UTs are also advised that if it is noticed that more funds are needed to implement the Scheme, due to an increase in the attendance of children, an increase in school working days or for any other reason, they may approach the Government of India with detailed justification seeking additional Central Assistance and food grains.Recommendation4.United Nations Organization (UNO) has declared the year 2023 as International Year of Millets which emphasizes on the nutritious values of millets. India has been traditionally the largest millet producer in the world. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Department should include more millets and coarse grains in diets of school going children of the country under PM POSHAN Scheme. The Committee also recommends the Department to learn from Best-Practices adopted by the States of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat regarding the inclusion of millets (SHRI ANNA) in the PM POSHAN Scheme.(Para 3.2.13 ibid)

5  
Action TakenThe Department has informed the Committee that a calendar of activities pertaining to this Ministry including quiz on my gov portal on importance of Millets, Debate/Group Discussion and rallies/nukkad-nataks among school children, etc. have been firmed up for the period 1st to 14th Oct, 2023 for the Celebration of International Year of Millets, 2023.It was also informed by the Department of School Education and Literacy that being a partner Ministry, Ministry of Education emphasis on the importance of Millets during Rashtriya PoshanMaah every year. In September, 2022, nearly 8.65 lakhs children were associated through Fairs, Rallies and Nukkad Nataks in Millet promotional activities under Rashtriya Poshan Maah.The Department further informed the Committee that the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations have also been requested to explore the possibility of introducing millets under PM POSHAN Scheme preferably in the districts where eating millets is a culturally accepted food habit. States/UTs have been suggested to introduce millet (Shri Anna) based menu once a week and also conduct cooking competitions among Cook-cum-Helpers to popularize millet based recipes. Small videos may be prepared for creating awareness about the goodness of millets and showcase them in schools and the consumption of millets may be discussed during the School Management Committees (SMCs) and Parent Teachers Meeting (PTM). States/UTs have also been advised to include the requirement of millets in their AWP&B for the year 2023-24. So far, the States of Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka and Assam have proposed millets in their Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) 2023-24.CENTRAL BOARD OF SECONDARY EDUCATION (CBSE)Recommendation5.The Committee observes that CBSE reviews the curriculum annually. However, the Committee is constrained to note that name of the unsung heroes of freedom movement from various parts of the country do not find adequate mention in curriculum being taught in classes IX-X to XI-XII. The Committee, therefore, strongly reiterates its recommendation at para 4.2.3 in its 347th Report on "Action Taken by the Government on the Recommendations/Observations contained in the Three Hundred Thirty First Report on Reforms in Content and Design of School Text Books" and 

6  
recommends that unsung heroes of freedom struggle from every part and community should find adequate mention in curriculum of class IX to XII students from next academic session.   (Para 4.2.4 ibid)Action TakenThe Committee has been informed that CBSE prescribes textbooks published by NCERT and prepares its syllabus for examination on the basis of the curriculum and textbooks of NCERT. The action regarding the content and design of school textbooks lies in the domain of NCERT. The schools affiliated to CBSE will implement the changes suggested by the Committee as and when introduced in the textbooks and curriculum by the NCERT.It was also informed that NCERT has taken note of the recommendation that unsung heroes of freedom struggle from every part and community should find an adequate mention in the curriculum of class IX- XII. Some of these revered personalities are already mentioned in textbooks in History of Classes X &XII, Themes in Indian History Part III NCERT has also informed that with the National Education Policy 2020 in place, the process of finalization of the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023 is going on. This document will help in the development of the new syllabus and textbooks.****

7

However, it is commendable that Department has made Single Nodal Account (SNA) functional in almost all States/UTs and hopes that fund utilization would improve from this Financial Year.   (Para 3.1.9 ibid)Action TakenThe Department has informed that the revised procedure of Single Nodal Account (SNA) is under implementation from 1stJuly, 2021. The Department is regularly interacting with States/UTs for effective implementation of SNA. Technical issues faced by the States/UTs in this regard are also taken up with MoF for their early resolution.Recommendation3.RTE Act, 2009 which led to insertion of Article 21-A in the Constitution of India has made Right of child to free and compulsory education of children in the age group of 6-14 years as a fundamental right. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should request and pursue with the concerned Ministry/Department to come onboard for setting up infrastructures

8  
required to hold online classes in the far flung and remotest areas in the country in order to ensure the benefits enshrined under RTE Act, 2009. At the same time it should be ensured that nutritional support reaches the beneficiaries involved in attending online classes.(Para 3.1.12 ibid)Action TakenThe Committee has been informed by the Department, that ICT and Digital Initiatives component of Samagra Shiksha covers Government and Aided Schools having classes VI to XII. Under this component financial assistance is provided for establishing ICT Lab and Smart Classrooms in schools. Online classes have been discontinued after Covid-19 pandemic becomenormal and now classes are being run as usual before the Covid-19. It was also informed that during the Covid-19 pandemic, the Ministry of Education had advised all States and UTs to provide Food Security Allowance comprising food grains and pulses, oil etc (equivalent to cooking cost) to all enrolled students in lieu of hot cooked meals under the Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Scheme, until the schools are reopened.PRADHAN MANTRI POSHAN SHAKTI NIRMAN (PM POSHAN) SCHEMERecommendation4.The Committee observes that during the financial year 2022-23 upto 16thFebruary, 2023, Rs. 7,337.91 crores have been utilized under PM-POSHAN scheme out of the allocated amount of Rs. 10,233.75 crores for the same in BE 2022-23. The Committee appreciates that under BE 2023-24, it has again been increased to Rs. 11,600 crores which is nearly 13.5% higher as compared to allocation under BE 2022-23 stage. The Committee observes that sufficient fund is available for PM-POSHAN Scheme as Centrally Sponsored Scheme and enhanced allocation for the same has been kept for the Financial Year 2023-24. Due to non receipt of proposals from certain States/UTs, utilisation gets hampered. The Department should extend assistance/guidance and encourage the most needy States by hand holding so that proposals are received timely from these States/UTs so that they are able to reap the benefits of this great initiative/scheme. The Committee appreciates the improvement in the situation of malnutrition, which was seconded by the NFHS-V as compared to NFHS-IV.(Para 3.2.7 ibid)

Action TakenThe Committee has been informed by the Department that interaction with States/ UTs is regularly being done by the Department for the timely submission of required documents/addressing the technical glitches, if any, for the timely release of funds.NEW INDIA LITERACY PROGRAMME (NILP)Recommendation5.crores which is 57% more as compared to allocation under RE 2022-23 stage.         (Para 3.3.7 ibid)Action TakenThe Department has informed that no comment is required.STRENGTHENING TEACHING-LEARNING AND RESULTS FOR STATES (STARS):Recommendation6.The Committee takes note of the budgetary allocations and utilization pattern during 2022-23and observes that as on 31st January, 2023, the Department has been able to spend Rs. 154.02 crores of the funds allocated at RE 2022-23 stage under the scheme. underutilization so as to take suitable measures to address the underutilization of allocated funds.   (Para 3.6.4 ibid)Action TakenThe Committee has been informed that the National Means Cum Merit Scholarship Scheme(NMMS) Scheme is covered under Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Periodical meetings are held with Officials of NIC-NSP and PFMS to ensure a better and smooth flow of funds to beneficiaryaccounts well in timeNATIONAL EDUCATION POLICY (NEP), 2020Recommendation9.The Committee observes that various stakeholders including various Ministries/Departments of Union Government, autonomous organizations and State Governments are involved, as education finds mention in concurrent list of Indian Constitution. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Education, particularly, Department of School Education & Literacy should take up the matter of implementation of NEP 2020 with various stakeholders, particularly all State Governments. The Committee, further, recommends that the impediments be identified and periodically reviewed. Further, the Department should coordinate with the stakeholders so that effective and expeditious implementation of NEP 2020 is made possible.(Para 3.7.5 ibid)10.    Abhiyan, UDISE+, Smart Class Programme which will cater to the goals envisaged by NEP 2020.(Para 3.7.6 ibid)Action TakenThe Committee has been informed that as per National Education Policy 2020, implementation of the Policy requires multiple initiatives and actions, which will have to be taken by multiple bodies in a synchronized and systematic manner. Therefore, the implementation of this Policy will be led by various bodies including the Ministry of Education, Central Advisory Board of 

12 
Education (CABE), Union and State Governments, education-related Ministries, State Departments of Education, Boards, National testing Agency (NTA), the regulatory bodies of school and higher education, National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERTs), schools, and Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs).It was also informed that NEP mentions various timelines for important Themes/subsets. The policy provides different timelines as well as principles and methodologies for its implementation. Accordingly, this Ministry has communicated to all States/UT Governments for taking steps for the implementation of NEP 2020 in letter and spirit. Moreover, Ministry and other implementing agencies under its purview have started taking initiatives towards the implementation of NEP 2020.The Department further apprised the Committee that to achieve the goals and objectives ofNEP 2020, the Department of School Education and Literacy has prepared a detailed NEPEducation) which was released on 8th April, 2021 linking recommendation of NEP with 297 tasks, responsible agencies to carry out the task, timelines and 304 outputs of the tasks.Further, the plan keeps in mind the concurrent nature of education and adheres to the spirit of federalism. States and UTs are given the flexibility to adapt this plan with local contextualization and also modify it as per their needs and requirements. This implementation plan delineates the roadmap and way forward for the implementation of NEP, 2020 for the next 10 years.SARTHAQ has been developed through a wide and intensive consultative process with States and UTs, Autonomous bodies and other concerned stakeholders. SARTHAQ is divided into two parts and has been uploaded on the Department's website under the links mentioned below: https://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files/SARTHAQ_Part-1_updated.pdf https://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files/SARTHAQ_Part-2_updated.pdfStates/UTs also report progress in identified tasks on a monthly basis. It was further informed that in order to ensure effective and efficient implementation of NEP 2020, the Department of School Education and Literacy has set up theme-wise implementation committees under the chairpersonship of concerned Joint Secretaries. States/UTs have also been requested to set up similar subject-wise implementation committees of experts, both to fine-tune implementation plans developed by them in accordance and in sync with SARTHAQ and to ensure implementation of the Policy as per the principles laid down in NEP 2020.

CHAPTER-IIIRECOMMENDATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEESAMAGRA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN1.The Committee observes that there are 9,86,565 vacancies of teachers against the sanctioned strength of 62,71,380 at the State Level, out of which, 7,47,565 posts at elementary level, 1,46,334 at secondary level and 92,666 at higher secondary level are vacant. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should encourage the State Governments to expedite the recruitment process to fill up the vacancies of teaching staffs in a time-bound manner to achieve 30:1 pupil-teacher ratio as envisaged under New Education Policy, 2020. It is also observed that in many States, teacher recruitment process is not transparent and is cumbersome. Therefore, the Committee recommends that Autonomous Teacher Recruitment Board should be formed at State level as recommended by some Education Committees.(Para 3.1.14 ibid)Action TakenThe Committee has been informed by the Department that education is a subject in the concurrent list of the Constitution and schools, other than those owned/funded by the Central Government are under the administrative control of respective State and (Union Territory Governments. Recruitment of teachers in these schools is the responsibility of the concerned State Government/Union Territory Administration. They may ensure that the entire recruitment process is transparent and completed in a time-bound manner. Further, vacancies keep arising due to factors like retirement, resignation and additional requirements on account of enhanced students' strength/new schools.It was also informed that the Department of School Education and Literacy, from time to time, through review meetings and advisories, requests the State and UT Governments for filling up vacant posts of teachers and their rational deployment. The Central Government through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, provides financial assistance to the States and UTs to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for various levels of schooling, as per norms prescribed in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, as amended from time to time.

16 
Comments of the CommitteeThe Committee notes the response given by the Department. The Committee is of the view that in order to achieve the vision laid out in New Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the Department should encourage the State Governments to expedite the recruitment process and for this the Department should interact and push for every State Government develop a detailed, time-bound action plan outlining the steps and deadlines to fill up the vacancies of teaching staff to achieve the 30:1 pupil-teacher ratio as per the New Education Policy, 2020. PRADHAN MANTRI POSHAN SHAKTI NIRMAN (PM POSHAN) SCHEMERecommendation2.In addition to a plethora of health and nutritional benefits, millets are also good for the environment with low water & input requirements hence being suitable for being grown even in harsh climates. The Committee recommends that the Department should conduct a fresh survey/evaluation in coordination with an independent agency especially in view of inclusion of millets (SHRI ANNA) under the scheme, so that, PM POSHAN Scheme could be consistently implemented in a better way and report of the survey becomes contextual, relevant and helpful in encouraging more students from disadvantaged backgrounds both, socially and economically to avail the benefit under the PM-POSHAN Scheme.(Para 3.2.12 ibid)Action TakenThe Department has informed the Committee in this regard as under:i. States and UTs have been requested to include millets (SHRI ANNA) once in a week under PM POSHAN scheme. So far, States of Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka and Assam have proposed millets in their Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) 2023-24.            ii. States and UTs have carried out cooking competitions involving cook cum helpers who have prepared new innovative recipes using different millets available in particular geographical regions.iii. Millet based exhibits displayed in the foyer of Talkatora Indoor stadium during the main event of Pariksha Pe Charcha 2023 on 27.01.2023 which was viewed by crores of people around the globe.

17 
iv. Millet based activities were carried out during the celebration of Rashtriya Poshan Maah in the month of September 2022. During this period, a Quiz competition on the MyGov portal was organized on Millets for school children. Rallies, group discussions, and debates were also held in schools among students on the use of millet.Comments of the CommitteeThe Committee notes and appreciates the various steps that are being taken by the Department for inclusion of Millets in the PM POSHAN Scheme. The Committee reiterates its recommendation for conducting a fresh survey/evaluation in coordination with an independent agency for the PM POSHAN Scheme in view of the thrust towards inclusion of millets (SHRI ANNA) under the scheme. The Committee is of the view that since the Scheme has been instrumental in addressing malnutrition and improving the nutritional status of children and pregnant women across the country, inclusion of millets in the scheme presents an opportunity to enhance the nutritional diversity and overall effectiveness of the program as Millets are known to be highly nutritious and can play a significant role in combating malnutrition among vulnerable populations. The Committee further states that some of the issues that can be addressed using the survey can be assessing the impact of millets inclusion on the nutritional intake and health outcomes of beneficiaries; identification of any implementation gaps that exist in various States in respect of Millet inclusion; level of awareness among the target population about the benefits with millets inclusion; analyze strategies to further encourage inclusion of socially and economically disadvantaged background citizens.
